senses.gloss:
शौभ शौभ, अस्, m. (fr. शुभ), a god, di-
vinity; the Areca or betel-nut tree (= गुवाक);
(अम्), n. the city of Hariścandra (fabled to be sus-
pended in the air, see हरि-श्-चन्द्र).

सौभ सौभ, अम्, n. (for शौभ), N. of
Hari-ścandra's city (suspended in mid-air); N. of a
town of the Śālvas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people.
—सौभ-पति, इस्, or सौभ-राज, अस्, m. the king
of Saubha or of the Saubhas.

शौभनेय शौभनेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शोभना),
sprung from a handsome mother; relating to any-
thing handsome or brilliant.

शौभाञ्जन शौभाञ्जन, अस्, m. (fr. शोभाञ्-
जन, q. v.), the tree Hyperanthera Moringa.

सौभाञ्जन सौभाञ्जन, अस्, m. = सोभाञ्-
जन, शोभाञ्जन, the tree Hyperanthera Moringa.

शौभिक शौभिक, अस्, m. (probably con-
[]
nected with शुभ), a juggler, conjurer (= इन्द्र-
जालिक).

सौभिक सौभिक, अस्, m. (for शौभिक), a
juggler.

शौभ्रेय शौभ्रेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-
longing to anything white or shining (e. g. to silver,
talc, sandal, &c.); (अस्), m. ‘son of Śubhrā,’ a patro-
nymic.
सौभकि सौभकि, इस्, m., N. of Drupada.

सौभग सौभग, अम्, n. (fr. सु-भग),
good luck, happiness; prosperity, riches, wealth.
—सौभग-त्व, अम्, n. a state of prosperity, hap-
piness.

सौभाग्य, अम्, n. auspiciousness, good fortune,
fortunateness, good luck; blessedness; beauty, grace,
charm; the happy and auspicious state of wife-hood
(as opposed to widowhood); affection, favour; con-
gratulations, good wishes; the fourth of the astor-
[]
nomical Yogas; red lead; borax (टङ्कण).
—सौ-
भाग्य-काण्ड, N. of part of the Atharva-veda.
—सौभाग्य-चिन्तामणि, इस्, m. a particular drug
or medicine compounded of various medicaments.
—सौभाग्य-चिह्न, अम्, n. any mark of good
fortune or blessedness; any sign or token of the
blessed state of wife-hood (e. g. red pigment on the
forehead, the marriage string, &c.).
—सौभाग्य-
तन्तु, उस्, m. the marriage string (which is cast
round the neck of the bride by the bridegroom at
the wedding and worn till widowhood).
—सौ-
भाग्य-तृतीया, f. the third day of the light half of
the month Bhādra.
—सौभाग्य-देवता, f. an
auspicious or tutelary deity.
—सौभाग्य-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, possessing good fortune or blessedness,
auspicious, fortunate; (अती), f. a married and un-
widowed woman.
—सौभाग्यवत्-ता, f. or सौ-
भाग्यवत्-त्व, अम्, n. auspiciousness, prosperity.
—सौभाग्य-वायन, अम्, n. auspicious offerings
of sweetmeats, &c.
—सौभाग्य-सुन्दरी-तीर्थ,
अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
सौभाग्य सौभाग्य. See col. 1.

सौभद्र सौभद्र, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सु-भद्रा),
belonging or relating to Su-bhadrā, q. v.; (अस्), m.
‘son of Su-bhadrā,’ epithet of Abhimanyu; (अम्),
n., scil. युद्ध, the war occasioned by the carrying
off of Su-bhadrā, q. v.

सौभद्रेय, अस्, m. a metronymic of Abhi-
manyu; Beleric Myrobalan (= विभीतक).

सौभर सौभर, अस्, m. a patronymic of
Kuśika (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 127).

सौभरि सौभरि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni
(married to the fifty daughters of Māndhātṛ and
father of 150 sons).

सौभरी सौभरी, f. (fr. सोभरि), Ved. a
verse composed by Sobhari.

सौभागिनेय 1. सौभागिनेय, अस्, m. (fr. सु-
भगा), the son of a favourite wife or of an
honoured mother.

सौभागिनेय 2. सौभागिनेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr.
सु-भागिनेय), belonging or relating to a good
sister's son.

सौभ्रात्र सौभ्रात्र, अम्, n. (fr. सु-भ्रातृ),
good brotherhood, fraternity.
